Definition: from G1909 and G5091; to tax upon, i.e. censure or admonish; by implication, forbid:--(straitly) charge, rebuke.
BiblicalUsage: Epitimáō means to rebuke — to speak sharply against, to charge with authority. Jesus rebukes the winds and the sea, rebukes unclean spirits, and rebukes Peter; Paul charges Timothy to reprove, rebuke, and exhort. It is correction with authority behind it, not mere scolding.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe epitimáō shows that rebuke belongs to love: Jesus rebukes what harms His people, and He commands His servants to do the same. I hold that a rebuke spoken in season is a mercy, not an insult.
RelatedEvents: Jesus Calms the Storm; Jesus Heals a Demoniac in the Capernaum Synagogue
